decisive_items: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum present
Lentiform fat signal mass between lateral wall of ascending thoracic aorta and medial wall of SVC
3.1 × 2.3 × 3.0 cm well-defined mass within the lower SVC with extension to the interatrial septum
response.rationale: The imaging shows a fat-signal mass involving the interatrial septum and compressing the SVC, which is characteristic of lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum, directly identified on TTE. Other candidates either describe the secondary compression (R9) or are unsupported tumor/metabolic diagnoses.

rejected.why: Superior vena cava syndrome is a clinical syndrome, not a specific diagnosis; the underlying cause is the lipomatous hypertrophy.
Cardiac lipoma is less specific; the TTE already identifies lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum.
Lymphoma is not supported by the fat-signal imaging characteristics.
Thyroid cancer metastasis is unlikely given the fat-signal mass and absence of other metastatic features.
Cardiac tumor is too broad and does not account for the specific fat-signal and interatrial septum involvement.
Hyperlipidemia-related cardiovascular disease is not supported by imaging or clinical findings.
Pulmonary embolism is not supported by the imaging or clinical presentation; no evidence of emboli.
